skillsOverview:
__TOC__
In Monsters & Memories, there are many skills your character can and learn and develop. How a skill works in game depends on the type of skill. Some skills are triggered automatically, while others are used at the player's discretion. Also, some skills are very general and shared by all, while others are specific to certain races and classes. In general, the more the character attempts to use a skill, the better he or she will become at it. == Skill List == === Bard Skills === Certain bard songs require certain instruments, and the better the minstrel is at playing these instruments, the more effective he or she will be at playing those songs. Each type of instrument learned, whether it is percussion, string, brass or wind, can improve the musician's effectiveness by enhancing their magical compositions. Bards (one can at least hope) also have great singing voices. And the better they are at this art, the more effective their songs, which are themselves often magical in nature. ====[[Skill_Brass_Instruments|Brass Instruments]]==== Skill tied to playing brass instruments, such as horns. ====[[Skill_Musicianship|Musicianship]]==== A skill describing the general musical capacity of a bard. ====[[Skill_Percussion|Percussion Instruments]]==== Skill tied to playing percussion instruments, such as drums. ====[[Skill_Singing|Singing]]==== Skill tied to performing songs with just the bard's voice. ====[[Skill_Stringed_Instruments|Stringed Instruments]]==== Skill tied to playing stringed instruments, such as lutes. ====[[Skill_Wind_Instruments|Wind Instruments]]==== Skill tied to playing wind instruments, such as flutes. === Combat Skills === ====[[Skill_Block|Block]]==== Negating an attack by deflecting the blow with one's body is a skill unique to the monk, and blocking is one of several skills available to that class. ====[[Skill_Defense|Defense]]==== The general ability to save one's own skin in melee combat. Raising your defense raises your AC. ====[[Skill_Dodge|Dodge]]==== One of the better ways to negate damage is to completely avoid the blow itself, and the skill of dodging allows the combatant to do just that. ====[[Skill_Double_Attack|Double Attack]]==== When a fighter becomes particularly adept at his craft, he may become fast enough to hit his opponent twice in the time it would normally take to hit once. Needless to say, this can be very advantageous in a difficult battle. ====[[Skill_Dual_Wield|Dual Wield]]==== Certain classes are able to wield a weapon effectively in both hands, thereby increasing the number of attacks and thus the amount of damage inflicted in a given period of time. ====[[Skill_Hand_to_Hand|Hand to Hand]]==== Although this skill can be mastered only by monks, most every other class can at least throw the occasional punch. Besides, one never knows when one might be relieved of one's weapon, both during combat and at other times. ====[[Skill_Offense|Offense]]==== The overall ability to inflict damage during combat. Raising Offense raises your Attack. ====[[Skill_Parry|Parry]]==== Ability to deflect blows with one's weapon. === Innate Skills === ====[[Skill_Acrobatics|Acrobatics]]==== The ability to perform acrobatic feats, from archers' Disengagement to rogues' Evade. It is also used for monks' Feign Death. ====[[Skill_Martial|Martial]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of combat. Grows with throwing skill and Taunt ====[[Skill_Might|Might]]==== One of several skills related to combat. Used for fighters' Frenzy and monks' Round Kick and Celestial Strike. ====[[Skill_Subterfuge|Subterfuge]]==== The ability to covertly affect targets using skills like rogues' Stealth or Rangers' Sneak. ====[[Skill_Valor|Valor]]==== The main skill pertaining to fighters' Offensive and Defensive Stances. It is also used for monks' Mend. === Non-Combat Skills === ====[[Skill_Alcohol_Tolerance|Alcohol Tolerance]]==== The ability to hold one's drink. ====[[Skill_Bind_Wound|Bind Wound]]==== The skill related to healing your wounds with bandages. Needs more information. ====[[Skill_Commerce|Commerce]]==== The skill related to buying and selling goods. Has a chance to increase when buying from and selling to NPC vendors. Needs more information. Humans seems to be the only Race so far who get an 10% Bonus at Vendors in Night Harbor. Elves seems to get an 10% Bonus in Faelindral. At least Woodelves but i guess it will count for all Elves. If other Races get their own starting Citys its possible they also get Discount in their Citys. ====[[Skill_Foraging|Foraging]]==== Allows you to find a random item on the ground. ====[[Skill_Riding|Riding]]==== The ability to purchase and ride [[Mounts]]. ====[[Skill_Sense_Heading|Sense Heading]]==== Allows you to determine what direction you are facing. ====[[Skill_Swimming|Swimming]]==== Many areas in the world of Eth-ur are covered by water, and one's ability to maneuver in that environment is directly related to one's skill level in swimming. As one becomes more adept at this skill, it is possible to move much faster in the water, and possibly even remain underwater for a bit longer as well. ====[[Skill_Tracking|Tracking]]==== Provides Druids, Rangers and Bards with the ability to identify nearby NPCs and navigate to them. === Spell Skills === ====[[Skill_Abjuration|Abjuration]]==== One of the several skills related to the art of magic, abjuration deals with defensive magic; for example, a spell that enables the character to take less damage from extreme cold. ====[[Skill_Alteration|Alteration]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of magic, alteration deals with changing things, whether it is illusion or an actual physical change. An example would be a spell that teleports something, or that enables a character to move faster, or forces him or her to move more slowly. ====[[Skill_Channeling|Channeling]]==== One of the several skills related to the art of magic, channeling allows you to continue casting without being interrupted if you are hit while casting the spell. ====[[Skill_Conjuration|Conjuration]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of magic, conjuration brings something from elsewhere into the world, whether they are elemental creatures or powerful clouds of energy. ====[[Skill_Divination|Divination]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of magic, spells of divination allow the caster to both detect things previously concealed and conceal things previously visible. ====[[Skill_Evocation|Evocation]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of magic, evocation deals with things that go boom. Fireballs, force spells, etc., all fall under the auspices of this offensive skill. ====[[Skill_Meditation|Meditation]]==== Another of the several skills related to the art of magic, meditation allows casters to memorize spells and regain their mana more quickly. === Weapon Skills === Combat is rather integral to the game, and there are a variety of weapons available to the combatant. In general, these weapons are broken up into three categories: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing, as well as whether they require one or two hands to wield. The higher the skill level, the more effective one is with that weapon. ====[[Skill_Archery|Archery]]==== In addition to the skills dealing with melee combat, range weapons are also prevalent in the world. The skill of archery deals with a character's efficacy in using bows, crossbows, and other, similar devices. ====[[Skill_Bludgeoning|Bludgeoning]]==== Hammers but maybe Maces with an update later. ====[[Skill_Piercing|Piercing]]==== Daggers and Spears ====[[Skill_Slashing|Slashing]]==== Swords and Axes . ====[[Skill_Throwing|Throwing]]==== Ability to use throwing weapons. Common weapons are the Dagger, Throwing Axe, Spear, and Shuriken. {{Navbox Skills}} [[Category:Skills]]

It focuses on breaking down herbs collected from [[Skill Herbalism|Herbalism]] and reagents to brew powerful temporary buffs, utilities, and crafting materials. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as an alchemist, visit a trainer: * '''Trainers:''' [[Alchemist Vizyl]] is located in Blackfeather Bazaar in [[Night Harbor]]. [[Alchemist Maverak]] is located in Western district in [[Underdocks]]. * '''Vendors:''' Next to Vizyl is [[an alchemist]] who sells the required flasks and vials, and will buy all excess cauldrons and ingredients. [[Veldara Stillflask]] is the supplier in Underdocks. == The Crafting Process == Alchemy consists of two distinct steps: # '''Grinding (Preparation):''' First, grind herbs and reagents into powder in a '''[[Mortar and Pestle]]''' container, which can be bought at the alchemy vendor. The [[Mortar and Pestle]] must be placed in a main inventory bag slot to be accessible. Once placed, open it like a bag and click the hammer icon on the right side to open the crafting menu. # '''Brewing (Combining):''' Second, combine your crafted powder with a vial inside a '''Cauldron''' to produce the final product. Temporary Cauldrons are player-made through the [[Skill Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]] tradeskill, while a permanent starter cauldron is available by visiting the alchemy vendor. == Ingredient Preparation ==

skills.Skill Bind Wound:
{{NeedsInfo}}

'''Bind Wound''' is one of the many [[tradeskills]] in ''[[Monsters & Memories]]''.

Players use a bandage item by right-clicking it while targeting themselves or another player. This acts as a channeled heal over time spell for 6 seconds. Movement or damage taken by the player applying the bandage will interrupt the bandaging process prematurely. A target can be bandaged while taking damage as long as they are not the player channeling the bandage heal. 

Applying a bandage to player also applies a 60 second debuff [[Recently Bandaged]], preventing the recently bandaged player from being bandaged again until the debuff expires. 

Bandages are made using the [[Skill Survival| Survival]] skill. 

== Getting Started ==
[[Medic Zafira]] is the bind wound trainer is located in the Sojourner's Camp in [[Night Harbor]]. Next to her is [[a medic]] which will buy all excess bandages.

[[Medic Florina]] is the trainer in [[Underdocks]], on the south side below the citadel.

== Healing ==

As of 2026-09-21, there are no recipes for Bind Wound.

Bind Wound skills are gained by applying bandages to players. 

Bind Wound skillups can be gained even if a player is at maximum health.

Higher tier bandages require a higher base player level to use.

It relies upon mined ore, corroded weapons and armor dropped by mobs, or scrap acquired via the breakdown of corroded items. Several recipes also require components crafted by [[Skill Tailoring|Tailoring]], [[Skill Leatherworking|Leatherworking]], and [[Skill Enchanting|Enchanting]]. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as a blacksmith, visit the trainers in the Night Market near the [[Forge]] and [[Anvil]]: * '''Trainers:''' [[Blacksmith Musafar]] or [[Weaponsmith Fahkri]] (Located in [[Night Harbor]]). [[Blacksmith Hargrul]] in Forge Row, on a lower terrace of the [[Underdocks]] citadel. '''Required Tools:''' * '''[[Smithing Pliers]]:''' Sold by blacksmith vendors. * '''[[Smithing Hammer]]:''' Granted to characters with the Blacksmithing non-combat [[Traits|trait]], or sold by vendors. * '''[[Rivet Cutters]]:''' Used to break down armor into their respective scraps. * '''[[Hammer and Chisel]]:''' Highly recommended for breaking down dropped weapons/armor into scraps.
'''💡 Progression Tip:''' Early Blacksmithing is heavily constrained by the supply of copper. Copper can only be found by mining nodes and [[Smelting]] the ore into bars, or buying from players. Vendors do not sell copper ore. Skill progress in early tiers is extremely slow—expect to level up only ~5 points per 50 white-tier combines. Once you reach the Bronze tier, supply opens up via mob drops.

skills.Skill Channeling:
Channeling governs how resistant a spellcaster is to being interrupted while being hit. The higher the skill, the more likely a spell will not be interrupted. Channeling can be raised to an overall score of 200, but is capped at a maximum for each level until reaching the level cap. It can be improved naturally through the act of casting spells while being hit or by paying a class trainer.

skills.Skill Commerce:
== Overview == The skill related to buying and selling goods. Has a chance to increase when buying from and selling to NPC vendors. Higher skill level reduces the purchase cost of items from merchants in addition to increasing the value of items sold to merchants. At skill level 25, the [[Haggle]] ability is unlocked and can be used to negotiate prices for items from Merchants. Skilling past level 25 can only be done by using the [[Haggle]] ability and then purchasing the haggled item (as of 2026-09-17). This can still work even if you "fail" the skill and make the vendor angry, increasing the price (verified 2027-10-08). == Notes == At 25 commerce, shady merchants will occasionally tell you if an item can be purchased and sold to another merchant elsewhere for a profit. [[File:Commerce Profit.png]] ==Classes== All classes begin with Commerce at level 1 and soft-cap at level 25, with a maximum possible skill of 100.

skills.Skill Disenchanting:
{| style="float: right; margin: 0 0 15px 15px; width: 280px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); font-size: 0.9em;" ! colspan="2" style="background: #2c3e50; color: #ffffff; font-size: 1.25em; padding: 12px; border-radius: 7px 7px 0 0; text-align: center;" | Disenchanting |- ! style="text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; color: #475569;" | Role | style="padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;" | Reagent Extraction & Magic Salvage |- ! style="text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; color: #475569;" | Trainers | style="padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;" | Disenchanter Kahni, Qaridi, Gwendyl |- ! style="text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; color: #475569;" | Locations | style="padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0;" | Night Harbor, Faelindral |- ! style="text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; color: #475569;" | Primary Tool | style="padding: 8px 12px;" | [[Disenchanting Cube]] |} '''Disenchanting''' is one of the many [[tradeskills]] in ''[[Monsters & Memories]]''. It serves as the primary gathering/salvaging profession for [[Skill Enchanting|Enchanting]], allowing players to break down magic-tagged items into magical powders and essences. == Getting Started == To begin your path as a disenchanter, visit one of the city trainers: * '''[[Night Harbor]]:''' [[Disenchanter Kahni]] (Spellbinders of the Spire) or [[Disenchanter Qaridi]] (on a balcony near the docks, near [[Vauquelin]] and [[an enchanter]]). * '''[[Faelindral]]:''' [[Disenchanter Gwendyl]] (above the Inn, near [[Enchanter Wyrel]] and [[Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter]]). * '''[[Underdocks]]:''' [[Disenchanter Gellar]] (in the blue-lit building south of the bank in Western district). '''Required Tools:''' * '''[[Disenchanting Cube]]:''' Sold by [[Enchanting Supplies]] vendors in major cities. == Mechanics & Usage ==
'''💡 Disenchanting Process:''' Place the [[Disenchanting Cube]] into an inventory bag slot. Place any item with a '''MAGIC''' tag into the cube and click 'Combine'. The cube will strip away the magical properties, yielding magical powder and rarely a magical essence.
* '''Failure Risk:''' Just like other tradeskills, you can fail a disenchanting attempt. If you fail, the item is completely destroyed and no reagents are recovered. * '''Quality Tiers:''' The quality and tier of the resulting magical powder depend on the item being salvaged (item level or attribute count). For full tier breakdowns, see the [[Skill Enchanting#Enchanting_Tiers|Enchanting Tradeskill Page]]. * ''Note: Items like the [[Cinder Beetle Shield]] that no longer possess a MAGIC tag cannot be disenchanted.'' == Disenchanting Yields ==

It relies upon resources harvested from [[Disenchanting]] magic items and metal bars created via [[Smelting]]. Enchanted bars are utilized by [[Skill Jewelcrafting|Jewelcrafting]], while reagents collected from disenchanting are used to create Enchanting Scrolls—consumable, tradable items that permanently add stat boosts to player equipment. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as an enchanter, visit one of the city trainers: * '''[[Night Harbor]]:''' [[Enchanter Haffiz]] is located in the Spellbinders of the Spire, next to the Enchanting tool (a bright purple orb from afar). * '''[[Faelindral]]:''' [[Enchanter Wyrel]] is located above the Inn (go up the ramp, bear left, follow signs) and above [[Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter]], alongside [[Disenchanter Gwendyl]]. * '''[[Underdocks]]:''' [[Requella]] is in the blue lit building next to the bank in Western district. '''Required Tools:''' * '''[[Tome of Enchantment]]:''' Sold by [[Enchanting Supplies|Enchanting Supply]] vendors in cities. * '''[[Trainee's Tome of Enchantment]]:''' Granted to characters with the Enchanter minor non-combat [[Traits|trait]]. * '''[[Enchanting Station]]:''' Located near enchanting trainers in major cities. * '''Recommendation:''' It is highly recommended to train [[Disenchanting]] and acquire a [[Disenchanting Cube]] at the same time. == Enchanting Mechanics & Tiers == === How Scrolls Work === * '''Usage:''' Right-click a scroll to make your hands glow with light blue smoke, then click an item to enchant it (can be interrupted by jumping or moving). * '''Trading & Vendors:''' Enchanted armor retains its enchant when traded to other players. Selling to a vendor removes the enchant, though it does not affect vendor buy price. * '''Restrictions:''' Equipment can only hold one enchantment at a time (new enchants overwrite old ones). * '''Failure Rate:''' Non-enchanter classes face a chance of failure when crafting scrolls inside the Tome of Enchantment. It allows players to harvest seafood and aquatic reagents from various bodies of water across the world. Fishing pairs exceptionally well with [[Skill Cooking|Cooking]], allowing you to turn your catches into substantial meals (e.g., combining Whitefish with Butter to make [[Pan Fried Whitefish]], which lasts considerably longer than standard rations). == Getting Started == To begin your angling adventures, you will need to acquire a pole and learn the skill from a trainer. === Equipment & Training === * '''Purchase a Pole:''' Travel to [[a fisherman (Night Harbor)]] or [[a fisherman (Faelindral)]] or [[Fishmonger Lyla]] (Underdocks, north side) to purchase a [[Fishing Pole]] for a modest fee. This item is mandatory to start fishing. * '''Equip the Pole:''' Open your inventory and place the Fishing Pole into your main weapon slot. Because it is a two-handed weapon, you must unequip your shield first. * '''Learn the Skill:''' In [[Night Harbor]], [[Fisherman Abduh]] is located on the end of the dock across from the fish monger NPC. There is also an "Expert Fisherman" across from the fishing supplies vendor on the dock. In [[Evershade Weald]], fishing supplies are at the base of the Traveler's Lift (noob lift), with the trainer nearby on the shore. In Underdocks you find [[Fisherman Dren]] on the north side below the citadel. Once you own a pole and train, the Fishing skill will appear in your Ability Book. * '''Prepare Bait (Optional):''' Return to Fishing Supplies and buy some [[Grub|grubs]] to use as bait. You can also find grubs with the [[Skill Foraging|Forage]] skill. === How to Fish === # Drag the Fishing skill icon from your Ability Book onto an empty slot in your hotbar. # Get close to any riverbank, lake shore, or coastal spot. ''(Note: Alongside the river in Evershade Weald will not work and returns "You cannot fish here").'' # Press the hotbar key assigned to Fishing to cast your line. # You don't need to perform any action to retrieve the line or the fish—everything is automatic!
'''💡 Beta Insights & Skilling Up (Aug/Sep 2026):''' * '''Baitless Fishing:''' You ''can'' fish without bait, though you will see a warning message. You can successfully catch [[Whitefish]] commonly (and [[Basa]] less commonly) without bait starting at a Fishing skill of 50. * '''Multi-Skillups:''' You can skill-up immediately upon casting your reel, and can receive multiple skill-ups during a single cast (up to 3 observed). * '''Leveling:''' It is suspected you can skill up to max level anywhere, but it slows down significantly at higher levels. (Confirmed baitless skillups all the way to level 91+).

Herbs collected from herbalism are used by [[Skill Alchemy|Alchemists]] to brew powerful potions.

[[Herbalist Jedesha]] is located in Western district in [[Underdocks]].

== Notes ==

Early leveling from 1 - 25 can be done by harvesting [[Lionleaf]] and [[Ghost Poppy]] in Night Harbor outside of North Gate and West Gate.
The next tier of leveling can be done by harvesting [[Ironroot]], [[Nomad's Grace]], and [[Whispering Sage]] in Shaded Dunes, in the Ashira Oasis behind the sand wall illusion.

It allows players to unlock the hidden power in precious stones by crafting powerful rings, earrings, and necklaces. Jewelcrafters accrue many of the gems they need from mineral veins, making it heavily synergistic with the [[Skill Mining|Mining]] gathering profession. Over time, jewelcrafting can also become a lucrative source of income. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as a jewelcrafter, visit one of the city trainers: * '''[[Night Harbor]]:''' Locate the jewelcrafting trainer to acquire the skill, then purchase your [[Jewelcrafting Kit]] from [[a jewelcrafter]] in the Night Market. * '''[[Faelindral]]:''' Find [[Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter]] alongside [[Enchanter Wyrel]] and [[Disenchanter Gwendyl]] up above the Inn (go up the ramp from the Inn, bear left, follow signs). All related suppliers are located nearby. * '''[[Underdocks]]''' Find [[Sorgen Stoneshiner]] at Forge Row in one of the lower terraces of the citadel. '''Required Tools:''' * '''[[Jewelcrafting Kit]]:''' The portable container used for basic combines. Sold by jewelcrafting vendors. * '''[[Trainee's Jewelcrafting Kit]]:''' Granted to characters with the Jewelcrafting minor non-combat [[Traits|trait]]. * '''[[Anvil]]:''' A stationary world object required to craft [[Chain Links]] using [[Smithing Pliers]].
'''💡 Quick Start Note:''' If you chose to start with the minor non-combat trait for jewelcrafting during character creation, you do not need to locate these NPCs—you are ready to craft immediately!

[[Seam Ripper]] |- ! style="text-align: left; padding: 8px 12px; color: #475569;" | Crafting Station | style="padding: 8px 12px;" | [[Leatherworking Station]] |} '''Leatherworking''' is one of the many [[tradeskills]] in ''[[Monsters & Memories]]''. It generally relies upon resources dropped by mobs or harvested from the world. Several recipes will also require components crafted by [[Skill Tanning|Tanning]], [[Skill Tailoring|Tailoring]], and [[Skill Enchanting|Enchanting]]. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as a leatherworker, seek out the leatherworking trainers in the city: - '''Trainers:''' [[Leatherworker Haiat]] in [[Night Harbor]] (the tannery). [[Leatherworker Keiros]] in [[Underdocks]] (citadel district, east side). - '''Vendors:''' Next to them are generic leatherworker NPCs who sell optional items and will buy your excess leather armor, hides, and thread. '''Required Tools:''' - '''[[Leatherworking Kit]]:''' The portable container used for basic combines (holds up to 6 items). Sold by leatherworker vendors. - '''[[Trainee's Leatherworking Kit]]:''' Granted to characters with the Leatherworking minor non-combat [[Traits|trait]]. - '''[[Seam Ripper]]:''' Used to break down dropped armor into scraps. - '''[[Leatherworking Station]]:''' A stationary world object required to craft advanced recipes that use more than 6 ingredients. == Learning Leatherworking == You can find the Leatherworking Trainer to learn the skill, or purchase a [[Leatherworking Kit]] and begin combining items to increase your skill naturally.
'''💡 Progression Tip:''' It is highly recommended to purchase a [[Seam Ripper]]. When combined with [[Tattered Rawhide]] armor in your kit, it produces [[Rawhide Scraps]]. This process continues into higher-level leather armors and is an excellent way to acquire extra materials for leveling up.
== General Leatherworking Notes == '''Upgrading Armor:''' During your adventures, you will kill undead and humanoid targets that drop [[Rawhide Scraps]] or [[Tattered Rawhide]] armor. You can upgrade these by combining the tattered armor with scraps in your kit to produce [[Patched Rawhide]] armor.

'''Inventory Management:''' Breaking down armor into scraps is a great way to 'consolidate' loot while your group is holding a camp far away from vendors, as individual scraps are much lighter than armor pieces.

'''Vendor Value:''' Patched Rawhide armor sells to vendors for significantly more than Tattered Rawhide armor, making this a good source of early income.

'''Synergy:''' Leatherworking has great synergy with [[Skill Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]], [[Skill Tailoring|Tailoring]], and [[Skill Tanning|Tanning]].

'''Farming Spots:''' Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane (near Nightharbor) and Ashira camps are great places for rawhide. On the Faelindral side, Blacktide Bay is excellent.

'''Note on Bags:''' Saddlebags '''CANNOT''' be used as bank bags. == Dropped Tattered Leather Sets == Humanoid mobs will occasionally drop level-equivalent raw tattered leather armor items. These items can be equipped as a quick temporary armor boost, refurbished through Leatherworking, or broken down into raw materials. List of dropped leather sets used as tradeskill materials: - [[Tattered Rawhide]] - [[Tattered Hide]] - [[Tattered Leather]] - [[Tattered Padded Leather]] - [[Tattered Thick Leather]] == Leatherworking Recipes ==

It serves as a primary gathering profession, allowing players to harvest raw wood and resin from nodes found throughout the forested areas of the world. Materials gathered are commonly refined by [[Skill Woodworking|Woodworking]] to be used in [[Skill Carpentry|Carpentry]] or [[Skill Fletching|Fletching]]. == Getting Started == To begin lumberjacking, you must acquire and equip a '''[[Lumberjack Axe]]'''. Once equipped, locate a wood pile—these nodes are often found scattered next to trees in the wilderness. Simply right-click on the wood pile to begin harvesting. Successfully harvesting a node will yield [[Wood]] and other materials based on the tier of the node. == Lumber Nodes & Locations ==

It serves as a primary gathering profession, allowing players to harvest raw metal ores, stones, and precious gems from mineral veins found throughout the world. Materials gathered are commonly refined by [[Skill Smelting|Smelting]] to be used in [[Skill Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]] or [[Skill Jewelcrafting|Jewelcrafting]]. == Getting Started == To begin your career as a miner, you must acquire the necessary tools and training. * '''Trainers:''' [[Miner Falmud]] is located in the Sojourner's Camp in [[Night Harbor]]. [[Jull Orbel]] is located in the Underdocks, in the Overreach area just east of the elevators. * '''Vendor & Tools:''' Next to Falmud is [[a miner]] who sells the required '''[[Mining Pick]]''' and the optional [[Mining Pouch]]. This vendor will also buy all your excess ores, stones, and gems. You can also buy a mining pick near the blacksmith trainer in the Underdocks. * '''How to Mine:''' Equip or carry your [[Mining Pick]], locate a mineral vein out in the world, and right-click on the node to begin harvesting.
'''💡 Leveling Tip:''' The hardest part of the early mining grind is graduating from Copper! To find early skill-ups, look for nodes at the West Gate (Night Harbor) and along the cliffs in the [[Shaded Dunes]].

It is the foundational process of refining raw ores mined from the earth—or recycling metal scraps—into usable metal bars for [[Skill Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]], [[Skill Jewelcrafting|Jewelcrafting]], and other crafts. == Getting Started == To begin your career as a smelter, you must acquire the necessary molds and find a workstation. * '''Trainer & Vendor:''' [[Smelter Jadid]], the smelting trainer, is located in the Night Market in [[Night Harbor]]. Next to him is [[a smelter]], a vendor who sells the various molds required for crafting. * '''Workstation:''' Visit a '''[[Forge]]''' to begin. Forges can be found in the Night Market and scattered around the city. * '''How to Craft:''' Left-click the [[Forge]] to open the crafting window, place your raw materials and mold into the slots, and press the Combine button. * '''Molds are consumed:''' Each combine uses up one mold, so a bar costs one mold ''and'' its ore -- molds are not reusable tools. Carry a stack to a [[Forge]]. Molds are sold by vendor NPCs in several cities; the [[Underdocks]] has none, so smelters there buy them elsewhere -- for example [[a smelter]] in the blacksmith building in the [[Night Harbor]] Night Market. Ensure you have at least 8 [[Wood]] (and optionally [[Resin]]) in your inventory, then click the hotkey to deploy it. Campfires can be used for cooking raw meats, and their duration can be extended by adding more wood directly to the fire!

It generally relies upon resources dropped by mobs or harvested from the world. Several recipes will also require components crafted by [[Skill Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]]. == Getting Started == To begin your journey as a tailor, seek out the tailoring trainers: {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding=5 style="border:1px solid #BBB; text-align: center; width:600px;" ! style="background-color: #faead3;"|Trainer Name!! style="background-color: #faead3;"|Location |- | [[Noura the Tailor]]|| [[Night Harbor]] (Night Market) |- | [[Flerri Dawntender the Tailor]] || [[Evershade Weald]] (Traders Terrace) |- | [[Yasmin Selvar]] || [[Underdocks]] (Crown Reach in the upper Citadel) |} Required Tools: {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding=5 style="border:1px solid #BBB; text-align: center; width:1000px;" ! style="background-color: #faead3;"|Tool Name!! style="background-color: #faead3;"|Sold By!! style="background-color: #faead3;"|Description |- | [[Tailoring Kit]] || [[a cloth armorer]] and [[Master Tailor Sansha]] || Used to craft on the go, holding up to 6 ingredients. |- | [[Trainee's Tailoring Kit]] || Granted to characters with the Tailoring minor non-combat [[Traits|trait]] || Used to craft on the go, holding up to 6 ingredients. |- | [[Seam Ripper]] || [[a cloth armorer]] || Used to break down armor into their respective scraps. |- | [[Loom]] || NA || A stationary world object required to craft advanced Tailoring recipes that use more than 6 ingredients. There is no Loom in the [[Underdocks]]. |} == Learning Tailoring == You can find the Tailoring Trainer to learn the skill, or purchase a [[Tailoring Kit]] and begin combining items to increase your skill naturally.
'''💡 Progression Tip:''' It is highly recommended to find a Tailoring Vendor such as [[Master Tailor Sansha]] and purchase a [[Seam Ripper]]. When combined with [[Tattered Cloth]] armor in your kit, it produces [[Cloth Scraps]]. This process continues into higher-level cloth armors and is an excellent way to acquire extra materials for leveling up.
== General Tailoring Notes == '''Upgrading Armor:''' During your adventures, you will kill targets that drop [[Cloth Scraps]] or [[Tattered Cloth]] armor. You can upgrade these by combining the tattered armor with scraps in your kit to produce [[Patched Cloth]] armor.

'''Inventory Management:''' Breaking down armor into scraps is a great way to 'consolidate' loot while your group is holding a camp far away from vendors, as individual scraps are much lighter than armor pieces.

'''Vendor Value:''' Patched cloth armor sells to vendors for significantly more than tattered cloth armor, making this a good potential source of early income.

'''Synergy:''' Tailoring has good synergy with [[Skill Leatherworking|Leatherworking]]. The [[Seam Ripper]] can be used to break down leather armor in a Leatherworking Kit. Tailoring products are also required as an input to the next higher tier of leather armor.

'''Self-Sufficiency:''' You can get to the point where you are crafting armor for your group in the field just from the items that you are picking up from dead enemies.

'''Farming Spots:''' Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane is a great place for cloth as well as Ashira camps. == Tailoring Recipes ==

html.Skill Alchemy:
Alchemy
Role Potions, Serums, Elixirs & Powders
Trainer Alchemist Vizyl, Alchemist Maverak
Location Night Harbor (Blackfeather Bazaar), Underdocks (Western district)
Primary Tool Mortar and Pestle
Crafting Station Cauldron

Alchemy is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It focuses on breaking down herbs collected from Herbalism and reagents to brew powerful temporary buffs, utilities, and crafting materials.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as an alchemist, visit a trainer:

  • Trainers: Alchemist Vizyl is located in Blackfeather Bazaar in Night Harbor. Alchemist Maverak is located in Western district in Underdocks.
  • Vendors: Next to Vizyl is an alchemist who sells the required flasks and vials, and will buy all excess cauldrons and ingredients. Veldara Stillflask is the supplier in Underdocks.

The Crafting Process

Alchemy consists of two distinct steps:

  1. Grinding (Preparation): First, grind herbs and reagents into powder in a Mortar and Pestle container, which can be bought at the alchemy vendor. The Mortar and Pestle must be placed in a main inventory bag slot to be accessible. Once placed, open it like a bag and click the hammer icon on the right side to open the crafting menu.
  2. Brewing (Combining): Second, combine your crafted powder with a vial inside a Cauldron to produce the final product. Temporary Cauldrons are player-made through the Blacksmithing tradeskill, while a permanent starter cauldron is available by visiting the alchemy vendor.

Bind Wound is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories.

Players use a bandage item by right-clicking it while targeting themselves or another player. This acts as a channeled heal over time spell for 6 seconds. Movement or damage taken by the player applying the bandage will interrupt the bandaging process prematurely. A target can be bandaged while taking damage as long as they are not the player channeling the bandage heal.

Applying a bandage to player also applies a 60 second debuff Recently Bandaged, preventing the recently bandaged player from being bandaged again until the debuff expires.

Bandages are made using the Survival skill.

Getting Started

Medic Zafira is the bind wound trainer is located in the Sojourner's Camp in Night Harbor. Next to her is a medic which will buy all excess bandages.

Medic Florina is the trainer in Underdocks, on the south side below the citadel.

Healing

As of 2026-09-21, there are no recipes for Bind Wound.

Bind Wound skills are gained by applying bandages to players.

Bind Wound skillups can be gained even if a player is at maximum health.

Higher tier bandages require a higher base player level to use.

Blacksmithing
Role Armor, Weapons, Shields & Metals
Trainers Musafar, Fahkri, Blacksmith hargrul
Location Night Harbor (Night Market), Underdocks (Forge Row)
Primary Tools Smithing Pliers
Smithing Hammer
Rivet Cutters
Crafting Station Anvil

Blacksmithing is one of the many Tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It relies upon mined ore, corroded weapons and armor dropped by mobs, or scrap acquired via the breakdown of corroded items. Several recipes also require components crafted by Tailoring, Leatherworking, and Enchanting.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as a blacksmith, visit the trainers in the Night Market near the Forge and Anvil:

  • Trainers: Blacksmith Musafar or Weaponsmith Fahkri (Located in Night Harbor). Blacksmith Hargrul in Forge Row, on a lower terrace of the Underdocks citadel.

Required Tools:

  • Smithing Pliers: Sold by blacksmith vendors.
  • Smithing Hammer: Granted to characters with the Blacksmithing non-combat trait, or sold by vendors.
  • Rivet Cutters: Used to break down armor into their respective scraps.
  • Hammer and Chisel: Highly recommended for breaking down dropped weapons/armor into scraps.

💡 Progression Tip: Early Blacksmithing is heavily constrained by the supply of copper. Copper can only be found by mining nodes and Smelting the ore into bars, or buying from players. Vendors do not sell copper ore. Skill progress in early tiers is extremely slow—expect to level up only ~5 points per 50 white-tier combines. Once you reach the Bronze tier, supply opens up via mob drops.

html.Skill Commerce:
Overview

The skill related to buying and selling goods. Has a chance to increase when buying from and selling to NPC vendors.

Higher skill level reduces the purchase cost of items from merchants in addition to increasing the value of items sold to merchants.

At skill level 25, the Haggle ability is unlocked and can be used to negotiate prices for items from Merchants.

Skilling past level 25 can only be done by using the Haggle ability and then purchasing the haggled item (as of 2026-09-17).

This can still work even if you "fail" the skill and make the vendor angry, increasing the price (verified 2027-10-08).

Notes

At 25 commerce, shady merchants will occasionally tell you if an item can be purchased and sold to another merchant elsewhere for a profit.

Disenchanting
Role Reagent Extraction & Magic Salvage
Trainers Disenchanter Kahni, Qaridi, Gwendyl
Locations Night Harbor, Faelindral
Primary Tool Disenchanting Cube

Disenchanting is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It serves as the primary gathering/salvaging profession for Enchanting, allowing players to break down magic-tagged items into magical powders and essences.

Getting Started

To begin your path as a disenchanter, visit one of the city trainers:

  • Night Harbor: Disenchanter Kahni (Spellbinders of the Spire) or Disenchanter Qaridi (on a balcony near the docks, near Vauquelin and an enchanter).
  • Faelindral: Disenchanter Gwendyl (above the Inn, near Enchanter Wyrel and Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter).
  • Underdocks: Disenchanter Gellar (in the blue-lit building south of the bank in Western district).

Required Tools:

  • Disenchanting Cube: Sold by Enchanting Supplies vendors in major cities.

Mechanics & Usage

💡 Disenchanting Process: Place the Disenchanting Cube into an inventory bag slot. Place any item with a MAGIC tag into the cube and click 'Combine'. The cube will strip away the magical properties, yielding magical powder and rarely a magical essence.

  • Failure Risk: Just like other tradeskills, you can fail a disenchanting attempt. If you fail, the item is completely destroyed and no reagents are recovered.
  • Quality Tiers: The quality and tier of the resulting magical powder depend on the item being salvaged (item level or attribute count). For full tier breakdowns, see the Enchanting Tradeskill Page.
  • Note: Items like the Cinder Beetle Shield that no longer possess a MAGIC tag cannot be disenchanted.

html.Skill Enchanting:
Enchanting
Role Equipment Scrolls, Bars & Scraps
Trainers Enchanter Haffiz, Wyrel
Locations Night Harbor, Faelindral
Crafting Station Tome of Enchantment Enchanting Station

Enchanting is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It relies upon resources harvested from Disenchanting magic items and metal bars created via Smelting. Enchanted bars are utilized by Jewelcrafting, while reagents collected from disenchanting are used to create Enchanting Scrolls—consumable, tradable items that permanently add stat boosts to player equipment.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as an enchanter, visit one of the city trainers:

  • Night Harbor: Enchanter Haffiz is located in the Spellbinders of the Spire, next to the Enchanting tool (a bright purple orb from afar).
  • Faelindral: Enchanter Wyrel is located above the Inn (go up the ramp, bear left, follow signs) and above Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter, alongside Disenchanter Gwendyl.
  • Underdocks: Requella is in the blue lit building next to the bank in Western district.

Required Tools:

  • Tome of Enchantment: Sold by Enchanting Supply vendors in cities.
  • Trainee's Tome of Enchantment: Granted to characters with the Enchanter minor non-combat trait.
  • Enchanting Station: Located near enchanting trainers in major cities.
  • Recommendation: It is highly recommended to train Disenchanting and acquire a Disenchanting Cube at the same time.

Enchanting Mechanics & Tiers

How Scrolls Work

  • Usage: Right-click a scroll to make your hands glow with light blue smoke, then click an item to enchant it (can be interrupted by jumping or moving).
  • Trading & Vendors: Enchanted armor retains its enchant when traded to other players. Selling to a vendor removes the enchant, though it does not affect vendor buy price.
  • Restrictions: Equipment can only hold one enchantment at a time (new enchants overwrite old ones).
  • Failure Rate: Non-enchanter classes face a chance of failure when crafting scrolls inside the Tome of Enchantment. Enchanter-class characters enjoy 100% success rates.

html.Skill Fishing:
Fishing
Role Catching Fish, Crabs & Reagents
Trainers Fisherman Abduh, Fisherman Dren, Expert Fisherman
Locations Night Harbor, Evershade Weald, Underdocks
Primary Tool Fishing Pole
Required Station Fishable Water Source

Fishing is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It allows players to harvest seafood and aquatic reagents from various bodies of water across the world. Fishing pairs exceptionally well with Cooking, allowing you to turn your catches into substantial meals (e.g., combining Whitefish with Butter to make Pan Fried Whitefish, which lasts considerably longer than standard rations).

Getting Started

To begin your angling adventures, you will need to acquire a pole and learn the skill from a trainer.

Equipment & Training

  • Purchase a Pole: Travel to a fisherman (Night Harbor) or a fisherman (Faelindral) or Fishmonger Lyla (Underdocks, north side) to purchase a Fishing Pole for a modest fee. This item is mandatory to start fishing.
  • Equip the Pole: Open your inventory and place the Fishing Pole into your main weapon slot. Because it is a two-handed weapon, you must unequip your shield first.
  • Learn the Skill: In Night Harbor, Fisherman Abduh is located on the end of the dock across from the fish monger NPC. There is also an "Expert Fisherman" across from the fishing supplies vendor on the dock. In Evershade Weald, fishing supplies are at the base of the Traveler's Lift (noob lift), with the trainer nearby on the shore. In Underdocks you find Fisherman Dren on the north side below the citadel. Once you own a pole and train, the Fishing skill will appear in your Ability Book.
  • Prepare Bait (Optional): Return to Fishing Supplies and buy some grubs to use as bait. You can also find grubs with the Forage skill.

How to Fish

  1. Drag the Fishing skill icon from your Ability Book onto an empty slot in your hotbar.
  2. Get close to any riverbank, lake shore, or coastal spot. (Note: Alongside the river in Evershade Weald will not work and returns "You cannot fish here").
  3. Press the hotbar key assigned to Fishing to cast your line.
  4. You don't need to perform any action to retrieve the line or the fish—everything is automatic!

💡 Beta Insights & Skilling Up (Aug/Sep 2026):

  • Baitless Fishing: You can fish without bait, though you will see a warning message. You can successfully catch Whitefish commonly (and Basa less commonly) without bait starting at a Fishing skill of 50.
  • Multi-Skillups: You can skill-up immediately upon casting your reel, and can receive multiple skill-ups during a single cast (up to 3 observed).
  • Leveling: It is suspected you can skill up to max level anywhere, but it slows down significantly at higher levels. (Confirmed baitless skillups all the way to level 91+).

Jewelcrafting (commonly referred to as JC) is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It allows players to unlock the hidden power in precious stones by crafting powerful rings, earrings, and necklaces. Jewelcrafters accrue many of the gems they need from mineral veins, making it heavily synergistic with the Mining gathering profession. Over time, jewelcrafting can also become a lucrative source of income.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as a jewelcrafter, visit one of the city trainers:

  • Night Harbor: Locate the jewelcrafting trainer to acquire the skill, then purchase your Jewelcrafting Kit from a jewelcrafter in the Night Market.
  • Faelindral: Find Vaelyndir the Jewelcrafter alongside Enchanter Wyrel and Disenchanter Gwendyl up above the Inn (go up the ramp from the Inn, bear left, follow signs). All related suppliers are located nearby.
  • Underdocks Find Sorgen Stoneshiner at Forge Row in one of the lower terraces of the citadel.

Required Tools:

  • Jewelcrafting Kit: The portable container used for basic combines. Sold by jewelcrafting vendors.
  • Trainee's Jewelcrafting Kit: Granted to characters with the Jewelcrafting minor non-combat trait.
  • Anvil: A stationary world object required to craft Chain Links using Smithing Pliers.

💡 Quick Start Note: If you chose to start with the minor non-combat trait for jewelcrafting during character creation, you do not need to locate these NPCs—you are ready to craft immediately!

Jewelcrafting Materials & Components

⚠️ Rule of Thumb: A standard 5-piece jewelry set typically requires 11 regular metal bars, 6 enchanted bars, and 5 gems. Use the tabs below to view component breakdowns, metal tiers, and gem tables.

html.Skill Leatherworking:
Leatherworking
Role Leather Armor, Containers & Mount Gear
Trainers Leatherworker Haiat, Leatherworker Keiros
Location Night Harbor (The Tannery), Underdocks
Primary Tools Leatherworking Kit
Seam Ripper
Crafting Station Leatherworking Station

Leatherworking is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It generally relies upon resources dropped by mobs or harvested from the world. Several recipes will also require components crafted by Tanning, Tailoring, and Enchanting.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as a leatherworker, seek out the leatherworking trainers in the city: - Trainers: Leatherworker Haiat in Night Harbor (the tannery). Leatherworker Keiros in Underdocks (citadel district, east side). - Vendors: Next to them are generic leatherworker NPCs who sell optional items and will buy your excess leather armor, hides, and thread.

Required Tools: - Leatherworking Kit: The portable container used for basic combines (holds up to 6 items). Sold by leatherworker vendors. - Trainee's Leatherworking Kit: Granted to characters with the Leatherworking minor non-combat trait. - Seam Ripper: Used to break down dropped armor into scraps. - Leatherworking Station: A stationary world object required to craft advanced recipes that use more than 6 ingredients.

Learning Leatherworking

You can find the Leatherworking Trainer to learn the skill, or purchase a Leatherworking Kit and begin combining items to increase your skill naturally.

💡 Progression Tip: It is highly recommended to purchase a Seam Ripper. When combined with Tattered Rawhide armor in your kit, it produces Rawhide Scraps. This process continues into higher-level leather armors and is an excellent way to acquire extra materials for leveling up.

General Leatherworking Notes

Upgrading Armor: During your adventures, you will kill undead and humanoid targets that drop Rawhide Scraps or Tattered Rawhide armor. You can upgrade these by combining the tattered armor with scraps in your kit to produce Patched Rawhide armor.

Inventory Management: Breaking down armor into scraps is a great way to 'consolidate' loot while your group is holding a camp far away from vendors, as individual scraps are much lighter than armor pieces.

Vendor Value: Patched Rawhide armor sells to vendors for significantly more than Tattered Rawhide armor, making this a good source of early income.

Synergy: Leatherworking has great synergy with Blacksmithing, Tailoring, and Tanning.

Farming Spots: Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane (near Nightharbor) and Ashira camps are great places for rawhide. On the Faelindral side, Blacktide Bay is excellent.

Note on Bags: Saddlebags CANNOT be used as bank bags.

Dropped Tattered Leather Sets

Humanoid mobs will occasionally drop level-equivalent raw tattered leather armor items. These items can be equipped as a quick temporary armor boost, refurbished through Leatherworking, or broken down into raw materials.

List of dropped leather sets used as tradeskill materials: - Tattered Rawhide - Tattered Hide - Tattered Leather - Tattered Padded Leather - Tattered Thick Leather

html.Skill Lumberjacking:
Lumberjacking
Role Harvesting Wood & Resin
Tool Required Lumberjack Axe
Target Nodes Wood Piles

Lumberjacking is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It serves as a primary gathering profession, allowing players to harvest raw wood and resin from nodes found throughout the forested areas of the world. Materials gathered are commonly refined by Woodworking to be used in Carpentry or Fletching.

Getting Started

To begin lumberjacking, you must acquire and equip a Lumberjack Axe.

Once equipped, locate a wood pile—these nodes are often found scattered next to trees in the wilderness. Simply right-click on the wood pile to begin harvesting. Successfully harvesting a node will yield Wood and other materials based on the tier of the node.

html.Skill Mining:
Mining
Role Harvesting Ores, Stones & Gems
Trainer Jull Orbel, Miner Falmud
Location Night Harbor (Sojourner's Camp), Underdocks (Overreach)
Primary Tool Mining Pick
Target Nodes Mineral Veins

Mining is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It serves as a primary gathering profession, allowing players to harvest raw metal ores, stones, and precious gems from mineral veins found throughout the world. Materials gathered are commonly refined by Smelting to be used in Blacksmithing or Jewelcrafting.

Getting Started

To begin your career as a miner, you must acquire the necessary tools and training.

  • Trainers: Miner Falmud is located in the Sojourner's Camp in Night Harbor. Jull Orbel is located in the Underdocks, in the Overreach area just east of the elevators.
  • Vendor & Tools: Next to Falmud is a miner who sells the required Mining Pick and the optional Mining Pouch. This vendor will also buy all your excess ores, stones, and gems. You can also buy a mining pick near the blacksmith trainer in the Underdocks.
  • How to Mine: Equip or carry your Mining Pick, locate a mineral vein out in the world, and right-click on the node to begin harvesting.

💡 Leveling Tip: The hardest part of the early mining grind is graduating from Copper! To find early skill-ups, look for nodes at the West Gate (Night Harbor) and along the cliffs in the Shaded Dunes.

Getting Started

Smelting
Role Metal Refining & Alloys
Trainer Smelter Jadid, Jedara Kilnwright
Location Night Harbor (Night Market), Underdocks (Forge Row)
Primary Tool Ingot Molds
Crafting Station Forge

Smelting is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It is the foundational process of refining raw ores mined from the earth—or recycling metal scraps—into usable metal bars for Blacksmithing, Jewelcrafting, and other crafts.

Getting Started

To begin your career as a smelter, you must acquire the necessary molds and find a workstation.

  • Trainer & Vendor: Smelter Jadid, the smelting trainer, is located in the Night Market in Night Harbor. Next to him is a smelter, a vendor who sells the various molds required for crafting.
  • Workstation: Visit a Forge to begin. Forges can be found in the Night Market and scattered around the city.
  • How to Craft: Left-click the Forge to open the crafting window, place your raw materials and mold into the slots, and press the Combine button.
  • Molds are consumed: Each combine uses up one mold, so a bar costs one mold and its ore -- molds are not reusable tools. Carry a stack to a Forge. Molds are sold by vendor NPCs in several cities; the Underdocks has none, so smelters there buy them elsewhere -- for example a smelter in the blacksmith building in the Night Harbor Night Market. (The Underdocks' own mold vendor, Mardah Stoneshiner, stocks jeweller's molds -- not smelting molds.)

Primary Tool Crafting: Survival (Ability)

Survival is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It is an essential utility skill that allows adventurers to craft bandages for healing, torches for light, and campfires for cooking and resting in the wilderness.

Getting Started

Unlike tradeskills that require a specific physical crafting bench, Survival crafting is accessed directly through your character's innate abilities.

  • Trainers & Vendors: Survival merchants and trainers can be found across from the Sageside bank and on the north wall of the Sojourner Camp in Night Harbor.
  • Crafting Items: Open your Ability Book, navigate to the Skills section, and click Crafting: Survival. Cast this ability to open the creation menu and begin crafting items.

💡 Building a Campfire: To build a campfire, open your Ability Book under skills and drag the "Campfire" icon to your hotbar. Ensure you have at least 8 Wood (and optionally Resin) in your inventory, then click the hotkey to deploy it. Campfires can be used for cooking raw meats, and their duration can be extended by adding more wood directly to the fire!

Tailoring
Role Cloth Armor, Bags & Components
Trainers Noura the Tailor, Flerri Dawntender, Yasmin Selvar
Location Night Harbor, Evershade Weald, Underdocks

Seam Ripper
Crafting Station Loom

Tailoring is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It generally relies upon resources dropped by mobs or harvested from the world. Several recipes will also require components crafted by Blacksmithing.

Getting Started

To begin your journey as a tailor, seek out the tailoring trainers:

Trainer Name Location
Noura the Tailor Night Harbor (Night Market)
Flerri Dawntender the Tailor Evershade Weald (Traders Terrace)
Yasmin Selvar Underdocks (Crown Reach in the upper Citadel)

Required Tools:

Tool Name Sold By Description
Tailoring Kit a cloth armorer and Master Tailor Sansha Used to craft on the go, holding up to 6 ingredients.
Trainee's Tailoring Kit Granted to characters with the Tailoring minor non-combat trait Used to craft on the go, holding up to 6 ingredients.
Seam Ripper a cloth armorer Used to break down armor into their respective scraps.
Loom NA A stationary world object required to craft advanced Tailoring recipes that use more than 6 ingredients. There is no Loom in the Underdocks.

Learning Tailoring

You can find the Tailoring Trainer to learn the skill, or purchase a Tailoring Kit and begin combining items to increase your skill naturally.

💡 Progression Tip: It is highly recommended to find a Tailoring Vendor such as Master Tailor Sansha and purchase a Seam Ripper. When combined with Tattered Cloth armor in your kit, it produces Cloth Scraps. This process continues into higher-level cloth armors and is an excellent way to acquire extra materials for leveling up.

General Tailoring Notes

Upgrading Armor: During your adventures, you will kill targets that drop Cloth Scraps or Tattered Cloth armor. You can upgrade these by combining the tattered armor with scraps in your kit to produce Patched Cloth armor.

Inventory Management: Breaking down armor into scraps is a great way to 'consolidate' loot while your group is holding a camp far away from vendors, as individual scraps are much lighter than armor pieces.

Vendor Value: Patched cloth armor sells to vendors for significantly more than tattered cloth armor, making this a good potential source of early income.

Synergy: Tailoring has good synergy with Leatherworking. The Seam Ripper can be used to break down leather armor in a Leatherworking Kit. Tailoring products are also required as an input to the next higher tier of leather armor.

Self-Sufficiency: You can get to the point where you are crafting armor for your group in the field just from the items that you are picking up from dead enemies.

Farming Spots: Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane is a great place for cloth as well as Ashira camps.

html.Skill Tanning:
Tanning
Role Pelt Refining & Canvas
Trainer Tanner Burhan
Locations Night Harbor, Faelindral, Keeper's Bight, Underdocks
Crafting Station Tanning Bucket

Tanning is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It is a refinement profession utilized to convert raw animal pelts into usable canvas materials for the Leatherworking tradeskill.

Getting Started

To begin your work as a tanner, seek out the trainer and gather your raw pelts to refine at a tanning bucket.

  • Trainers: Tanner Burhan, the tanning trainer, is located in the Tannery in Night Harbor. Tanner Paluvian is below the citadel, east side, in Underdocks.
  • Vendors: Next to Burhan is a tanner, a merchant who will buy all of your excess hides, leather, and thread.

💡 Crafting Tip: When converting pelts into canvas, you must place them into the Tanning Bucket one at a time before pressing craft. The output quantity of canvas is based on the quality of the pelt. Note that obtaining these pelts directly from beasts currently does not require a specialized skinning skill!

Woodworking
Role Lumber Refining & Boards
Training Station-Based (No Trainer)
Location Night Harbor (Shipyard)
Crafting Station Sawmill

Woodworking is one of the many tradeskills in Monsters & Memories. It refines raw lumber gathered via the Lumberjacking skill into usable boards and components required for Carpentry.

Getting Started

Unlike many other tradeskills, Woodworking has no traditional trainer; instead, it relies entirely on the use of stationary world workstations called **Sawmills**.

  • Night Harbor Location: The sawmill is located at the shipyard, situated directly in front of the forge and Carpenter Quais.

Skill Progression & Trivial Scale

💡 Progression Note: Elder Wood Panel Board, Ironbark Board, and Wood Board all share identical trivial progressions across skill levels:

  • Yellow at Woodworking 1
  • White at Woodworking 4
  • Dark Blue at Woodworking 11
  • Light Blue at Woodworking 18
  • Green (Trivial) at Woodworking 25
